To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the motion capture camera system can interfere with the Microsoft Kinect v 1 sensor.

the motion capture interferes with Microsoft Kinect v2 sensor's performance in skeleton tracking and the retroreflective markers cause the Microsoft Kinect v 1 to give an incorrect estimation of the joint position.
the Microsoft Kinect v 1 sensor is not affected by the Qualisys motion capture cameras and retroreflectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of a marker based system on the Microsoft One Kinect v2 sensor.
the interference of a motion capture camera system on the Microsoft Kinetic v2 sensor's performance and the impact of retroreflective markers on the Microsoft Kinect sensor's performance.
the influence of a marker based system on the performance and accuracy of Microsoft Kinect v1 and v2 sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a motion capture system can have a negative effect on the performance of the Microsoft Kinect v 1 and Microsoft Kinect v 3.
the Microsoft Kinect v 1 and 2 are not suitable for use with motion capture systems, and the use of motion capture systems with Microsoft Kinect v 3 should be investigated.

Microsoft Kinect v2 sensor is sensitive to retroreflective marker based motion capture cameras, and it is suggested that researchers should avoid placing retroreflective markers in the proximity of Microsoft Kinect v1 or v2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Microsoft Kinect v 1 is more robust to the presence of motion capture systems compared to Microsoft Kinect v2.
Microsoft Kinect v2 is not suitable for use in a motion capture environment.
the Microsoft Kinect v1 and v2 are not suitable for kinematic studies in a lab with marker based motion capture equipment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should be aware of the impact of the motion capture system on Microsoft Kinect v2 performance and take the required steps to avoid such interference.
researchers should be aware of this potential source of error when conducting motion capture experiments using the Microsoft Kinect v 1 and 2.
the motion capture cameras and retroreflectors may cause a timevarying error in the Microsoft Kinect estimate and hence should be avoided.
